The Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China (the Alliance) case, in which the defendants were convicted of "inciting subversion of state power," will see sentencing submissions tomorrow (the 28th). Former Alliance standing committee member Tang Ngo-kuen began queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts yesterday (the 26th), and this morning (the 27th) at around 11 am, suspected queue stand-ins appeared.

The suspected queue stand-ins, numbering around 50 to 60 people, registered their details in front of a police-set-up tent before entering the cordon area to queue. Some pulled along trolley suitcases, others brought yoga mats, and several people, seemingly by coincidence, entered carrying the government's green garbage "designated bags."

The "designated bag" is a "product" the government rolled out last year as it prepared to implement the waste charging scheme. Due to insufficient supporting measures, the policy triggered a public backlash on the eve of its implementation. Last September, citing major challenges such as a "global trade war" and "an increasingly complex geopolitical landscape," the government said it needed to formulate waste reduction and recycling policies in line with the times, and announced that the current-term administration would "maintain the suspension" of the waste charging scheme. Last October, the stockpile of "designated bags" reached 170 million. The government said at the time that it would distribute them free of charge to public housing tenants on a monthly basis for six months.

The Alliance, along with former chairman Lee Cheuk-yan, former vice-chairman Albert Ho, and Chow Hang-tung, were charged with "inciting subversion of state power." The Alliance, Lee Cheuk-yan, and Chow Hang-tung pleaded not guilty and were convicted last Friday (the 21st). Sentencing submissions for all defendants are scheduled for this Friday (the 28th).
